## Seat ruling · #29434 route · 2026-11-02T21:02Z

Ruling-ref: the card thread's measurements and options (project file `server-seat3/29434-route-options.md`, measured on `origin/main` `2420778c`); the seat delta ("report options before adding one; new public names are the seat's call"); the maintainer's standing word that lane seats decide technical sequencing and grading (2026-11-01T12:11Z).

**Q1, the route: (c). The instance `auth` is applied to stdio as one named env var, spelled `providerConfig.transport.credentialEnv`.**

- Why (c): it is the only option that leaves the secrets layer whole. The materializer already resolves `entry.auth.credentialRef`. It degrades an instance whose reference no arm answers, naming the reference and no value. It fingerprints the source into the signature, so a credential write re-spawns the server, and it lists the reference in Setup. Options (a) and (b) would put references where the materializer cannot see them. They would also need a resolver hunk on `ConnectorProviderContext` (a schema face), and (a) fails the read test because `transport.env` is withheld whole. ADR-0097 §3 keeps the materializer provider-agnostic, and (c) uses it as it stands.
- The name `credentialEnv` is ruled. It is provider-owned `providerConfig` vocabulary (ADR-0023), so there is no spec key: `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, as claimed.
- Cost accepted: one secret per instance. A server that needs two secrets keeps the second in `env`, or is split into two instances.
- The four configuration refusals in the options file are in scope. They are: a `credentialEnv` that is not a valid env-var name, `credentialEnv` on an http transport, `credentialEnv` with no static `auth`, and `credentialEnv` naming a variable that `transport.env` also sets. None of them puts a value in its message. They are new refusals only of the new key, so nothing that is accepted today moves.

**Q2, `auth` on stdio without `credentialEnv`: A. Leave the runtime as it is on this card; the seat files the silent drop as its own card.**

- Refusing it here would make this PR a narrowing and BREAKING for apps that declare `auth` beside a literal `env`. That decision belongs on its own card, with the options measured against apps in the field.

Face: the declaration face at `TIER_DEFAULT` under (c), if `record-recognisers.mjs --paths` agrees on the final file list. Build now.

## Claim amendment · #29434 · 2026-11-02T22:24Z

Branch: `claude/project-thread-439xd1` (unchanged)
Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: added

Why: the contract review on PR #29621 (head `f3ff3349`, verdict FAIL on this point alone) is right, and it corrects the seat's own route ruling (`6588385697`, which said `none`).

- AGENTS.md changeset rule 3 defines the kind as the change to what a metadata author can write: a new key is `added`.
- `providerConfig.transport.credentialEnv` is a key an author writes in a connector entry. That it is provider-owned (ADR-0023) explains why there is no spec hunk. It does not make the key unauthorable.
- Precedent: PR #27387 added `providerConfig.include` to `connector-openapi` with no spec hunk and declared `added`.
- The level follows the kind: `@objectstack/connector-mcp` takes `minor`. `@objectstack/lint` changes message text only and may stay `patch`.

File surface also adds `.changeset/29341-connector-credential-literal.md`. That changeset is still pending on `main`, and its stdio bullet ("a stdio MCP server takes no `auth`") would ship in the same release as the opposite statement. Its stdio sentence is corrected on this PR, as a prose edit to another card's pending changeset (the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class). The route ruling stands otherwise.
